title: deliver_later enqueued inside the transaction can run before commit
rationale: ReceiptMailer's documented contract states deliver_later enqueues on a separate connection, so the job can run before the surrounding transaction commits and read an Order that does not exist yet, raising RecordNotFound. The enqueue must happen after commit; this will intermittently fail to send receipts and raise on the job worker.

title: Query ignores the request context, so abandoned requests keep running their query
rationale: Using context.Background() means a cancelled or timed-out client request still runs the query to completion, holding a database connection that request cancellation would otherwise release. Passing r.Context() ties the query lifetime to the request.

title: Query result is never closed if Store.Query returns database/sql rows
rationale: If Store.Query returns sql.Rows, the rows are never Closed, leaking a connection per request. This finding rests on an assumption about the unshown Store.Query contract; if it returns a fully-materialized slice, there is no issue.

title: URLs built from slugs are no longer unique, breaking the previous guarantee
rationale: Previously the URL embedded the unique id, so every published post got a distinct URL. Building it from the title means two posts published with the same title (or, depending on text.Slug, an empty or all-punctuation title yielding "/posts/") now produce identical URLs, breaking any lookup or routing that assumed URL uniqueness. If slug collisions are handled elsewhere that should be stated; nothing shown does.

title: Empty-slug titles can produce a bare "/posts/" URL
rationale: The old code produced a URL for every integer id, including 0 and negatives (itoa handled 0 explicitly). If text.Slug returns an empty string for some titles, Publish now yields the bare prefix "/posts/" with no slug, a URL form that did not previously exist. The exact behavior depends on text.Slug, which is not shown; if it guarantees a non-empty result this can be dropped.

title: Slug-based URLs are no longer unique across posts
rationale: The slug is derived from the title, so two posts with the same title — or titles that slug identically, such as "Hi!" and "hi" — now get identical URLs where the previous id-based scheme was unique by construction. Any caller or route that treats Post.URL as a unique key for lookups or storage will collide.

title: Empty or fully-stripped titles yield a bare "/posts/" URL
rationale: If text.Slug returns an empty string for a title that is empty or contains no sluggable characters, Publish produces the degenerate URL "/posts/". This input is directly reachable via Publish's signature, but the consequence rests on Slug's behavior for such input, which was not shown.

title: total() applies toCents to a value already denominated in cents
rationale: LineItem.priceCents is documented as an integer number of cents, yet total() passes it through toCents before multiplying. This rests on an assumption about toCents' behavior in money.ts (not shown): if it converts dollars to cents, every total is inflated 100x; if it is a validation/rounding helper, the call is redundant but the intent is unclear. The charge amount depends on confirming toCents' contract.

title: total() double-converts a value that is already in cents
rationale: LineItem documents priceCents as an integer number of cents, and describe() uses it directly with formatCents. Passing it through toCents() here applies a second conversion, so the total will not match the per-line amounts shown on the receipt (a $5.00 item would total 50000 if toCents converts dollars to cents). Use the value directly: sum += item.priceCents * item.quantity.

title: Quote handler awaits client.price without error handling
rationale: client.price performs a network call to the pricing service and can reject; with no error handling in the handler, a failure surfaces as an unhandled rejection and the request never receives a response instead of a 5xx.

title: No error handling around client.price leaves the response unanswered on failure
rationale: client.price is a network call that can reject on timeout or non-2xx; the rejection escapes quote, so res.json never runs and the request hangs or becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Wrap the call in try/catch and return an error response.

title: Client created per request
rationale: A new client is constructed on every request; if createClient allocates a connection pool or keeps sockets open, quote leaks one per request. Hoisting it to module scope (as PRICING_URL already is) reuses one instance. If createClient is stateless and cheap, this is moot.

title: Retrying a card charge on timeout risks duplicate charges
rationale: A timeout does not mean the charge was not processed, so a retry that succeeds after an ambiguous failure double-charges the card. `with_retry` must either limit retries to errors that provably precede the request or pass an idempotency key to `gateway.charge`.

title: Unverified key access: claims["sub"] raises KeyError when the token has no sub claim
rationale: claims["sub"] assumes verify always returns a claims dict containing that key. Verify's implementation was not shown, so if a token without a sub claim verifies successfully, the KeyError escapes as a 500 instead of the documented (None, error_response) contract. This rests on the unshown behavior of verify.

title: Plaintext API key logged to audit log
rationale: The plaintext API key is written to the audit log. The module's own contract states the key is shown once and stored only as a hash; an audit log line persists the secret, so anyone with log access (log aggregation, retention, off-host shipping) obtains a working credential. Audit events should record key_id only.

title: Plaintext API key written to audit log
rationale: The full plaintext API key is passed to the audit log, contradicting the function's contract that the key is shown once and stored only as a hash. Audit logs typically persist and ship off-host, so anyone with log access obtains a usable credential.

title: Non-idempotent charge is retried on timeout, risking duplicate charges
rationale: A timeout does not tell the caller whether the processor completed the first attempt, so a retry can produce two charges for one purchase. The rating rests on what the diff does not show: whether with_retry re-attempts after timeouts and whether gateway.charge is idempotent; if either already protects against this, the defect does not materialize.

title: New client is created per request, leaking sockets
rationale: createClient is documented as expensive and long-lived: it opens eight keep-alive sockets and none are closed until process exit. Creating one per request leaks eight file descriptors per call and will exhaust the file descriptor table under load, making the service fail after a bounded number of requests. Create a single client at module scope (or startup) and reuse it.

title: Plaintext API key written to audit log shipped off-host
rationale: The full plaintext API key is passed as an audit field, and app/audit.py serialises every field verbatim to stdout for off-host SIEM retention readable by the whole security organisation — directly violating that function's documented prohibition on passing credentials. This is a guaranteed production leak of a secret that is supposed to be shown once and stored only as a hash.

title: No authorization check on the account parameter
rationale: The handler reads the account parameter and queries its totals with no authorization check visible in the handler. If no upstream middleware enforces per-account access, any caller can read any account's data; if such middleware exists, this is already handled. Fixing this in or beside the handler makes the guarantee explicit.

title: Query ignores the request context
rationale: Using context.Background() instead of r.Context() means a cancelled or timed-out client request leaves the database query running and holds the connection until it completes. Demonstrated directly by the code shown.

title: 500 error written after a partial response
rationale: If the store call succeeds but json.Marshal or the response write fails, http.Error writes a 500 when headers may already have been sent, producing a malformed response the client cannot parse reliably.

title: Error message handling (no defect reported)
rationale: This reviewer finding confirms internal error details are not leaked to the client; no defect is described.

title: Unvalidated account value written to logs
rationale: Account identifiers from user input are logged verbatim; a value containing newlines could forge log entries. Consequence depends on the logging backend and any downstream log sanitation, which was not shown.

title: json.Marshal error handling (no defect reported)
rationale: This reviewer finding reports that the marshal error is handled correctly; no defect is described.

title: Content-Type ordering (no defect reported)
rationale: This reviewer finding confirms the Content-Type handling is correct; no defect is described.

title: No rate limiting on the report endpoint
rationale: No rate limiting is visible in the handler, which could allow bulk scraping of accounts; this assumes no rate-limiting middleware exists upstream, which was not shown.

title: No cache-control headers on financial data responses
rationale: Responses carry no cache-control headers, so intermediaries could cache account-level totals. The practical exposure depends on deployment topology and existing header middleware, which was not shown.

title: Write error ignored
rationale: Ignoring the w.Write return value means a truncated response body is not detected or logged. The write is the last step, so the client receives the failure regardless; the cost is lost diagnostics only.

title: Receipt email is enqueued inside the transaction and can be sent for a rolled-back order
rationale: deliver_later enqueues the mailer job inside the transaction. If any statement after line 11 (or the commit itself) fails and the transaction rolls back, the job is already queued and will attempt to deliver a receipt for an order that no longer exists, producing a failed job — or, if the row is merely invisible to it, a spurious send. Enqueueing after the transaction commits (e.g., via an after_commit hook) removes the hazard.

title: Expired tokens are accepted as valid authentication
rationale: tokens.verify's documented contract requires every caller other than the refresh endpoint to call is_expired(claims) before trusting the result, and current_user never does. A client holding an expired token gets a valid (user_id, None) response, so expired credentials authenticate successfully.

title: current_user accepts expired tokens
rationale: verify() returns claims of expired tokens by design, and its contract requires every caller to check is_expired(claims). current_user skips that check, so an expired token yields a valid user_id instead of a 401, defeating token expiry.

title: KeyError on a signed token without a sub claim
rationale: verify() returns the parsed claims whenever the signature is valid, and nothing guarantees a "sub" key is present, so claims["sub"] raises KeyError for a signed token lacking it. If token issuance (not shown) always sets sub, this is unreachable in practice; if it can be absent, this should return a 401.

title: Cache.Get error is silently ignored
rationale: The error from Cache.Get is discarded, so a real cache-backend failure (connection error, timeout, corruption) is indistinguishable from a miss: the page is re-rendered and re-Put on every request, and any monitoring on Get errors is bypassed. This rests on the assumption that Get only errors in conditions that cannot occur for this backend, which the shown code does not establish.

title: Retrying a non-idempotent charge can double-charge the card on timeouts
rationale: with_retry's contract requires its callback to be idempotent and explicitly warns that retrying a card charge can charge the customer twice when the first attempt times out after the processor has accepted it. Wrapping charge without establishing idempotency makes a double charge reachable, not hypothetical.

title: Full plaintext API key written to audit log
rationale: The full API key is passed to audit(), which serialises every field verbatim to stdout that ships off-host and is readable by the whole security organisation. audit()'s own contract explicitly forbids passing credentials as fields; this logs a live secret that is supposed to be shown to the user once and stored only as a hash.

title: Cache.Get error is silently discarded
rationale: Discarding the error from p.Cache.Get makes a cache failure indistinguishable from a miss, so requests silently re-render and re-Put while the backend errors, with no signal the cache is unhealthy. This rests on the assumption that Get's error can indicate more than a miss; if it is only a miss indicator, the impact is negligible.

title: settle retries a non-idempotent charge, risking duplicate charges
rationale: A charge that times out after the processor accepted it will be submitted again, double-charging the customer on a path the docstring says runs several times a day. with_retry's contract requires fn to be idempotent; Gateway.charge is not, and the code adds no idempotency key or receipt lookup to make the retry safe.

title: Delay converted to seconds but schedule() expects milliseconds, firing jobs 1000x too early
rationale: schedule() takes delayMs in milliseconds (per its documented contract and setTimeout), but registerDelayed divides parseDuration's millisecond result by 1000 and passes it as the millisecond delay. A "5m" delay becomes 300 ms, so jobs run 1000x too early. The docstring's claim that the delay is converted to seconds for schedule() contradicts schedule's own contract.

title: Cache.Get error is silently dropped
rationale: Discarding the error from Cache.Get makes a failing cache backend indistinguishable from a miss: every request re-renders and re-Puts, and nothing logs the failure. The fallback behavior is acceptable, but the error should be surfaced (e.g., logged) so operators can distinguish a slow cache from a broken one.

title: User-supplied filename is passed to save(), which silently overwrites existing files
rationale: `save` overwrites silently, and its contract requires callers to check `exists()` and refuse or rename whenever the filename is user-supplied. Here the filename is user-supplied, so a second upload with the same name destroys the first file with no error.

title: Per-user directory is assumed to exist but never created
rationale: `save` opens the path directly and creates no directories, so the first upload for a user whose directory does not exist will raise FileNotFoundError and return a 500. This rests on the assumption that no other component pre-creates the per-user directory, since nothing in the shown code creates UPLOAD_DIR/<user_id>.

title: Query ignores request cancellation by using context.Background()
rationale: The query uses context.Background() instead of r.Context(), so a client that disconnects does not cancel the in-flight database query; slow or abandoned requests keep consuming database resources.

title: Cleanup deletes every upload when called with no query parameters
rationale: With neither parameter supplied, the filter is empty and DeleteWhere matches every row, deleting the entire uploads table on a single request with no parameters — the store's contract explicitly requires callers to refuse an empty filter. A stray `DELETE /admin/uploads` becomes an unrecoverable mass deletion.

title: Publish can emit the URL "/posts/" for titles that slug to empty
rationale: Slug returns "" for titles with no letters or digits (e.g. "???"), and its contract requires callers to check for that. Publish does not, so such posts get the bare collection URL "/posts/" and all collide on the same page, where previously every post had a unique id-based URL.

title: quote creates a new pricing client per request, leaking eight sockets per call
rationale: createClient's contract is one client per process, shared across calls; creating a client per quote request opens eight keep-alive connections that are never closed, so every request leaks sockets until the file descriptor table is exhausted under traffic. Create one client at module scope next to PRICING_URL and reuse it in the handler.

title: Handler serves any HTTP method, not just GET as documented
rationale: The comment documents GET /pages/{slug}, but the handler never checks r.Method, so POST, PUT, DELETE, and other methods all receive rendered page bodies and populate the cache. This holds unless the route registration restricts methods, which the shown code does not demonstrate.

title: Empty-string sentinel conflates cache miss with cached empty content
rationale: The empty string serves as both the miss sentinel and a possible render result, so a cache entry stored via Put is indistinguishable from a miss and the slug re-renders on every request. Independently, Get's error is swallowed and treated as a miss, so a cache-layer failure surfaces only as unbounded re-rendering rather than an error signal.

title: total() converts already-cent values through toCents, inflating sums 100x
rationale: `LineItem.priceCents` is already an integer number of cents, but `total` passes it through `toCents`, which expects dollars and multiplies by 100. The returned total is 100x the correct charge, so every cart would be overcharged. Use `item.priceCents` directly.

title: total() applies toCents to values that are already in cents
rationale: LineItem.priceCents is documented as an integer number of cents, while toCents is documented as converting a dollar amount and explicitly must not be applied to values already in cents. Passing priceCents through toCents corrupts the computed total for every item.

title: Delay divided by 1000, but schedule() takes milliseconds
rationale: schedule(fn, delayMs) takes milliseconds, as its parameter name and contract indicate, but the delay from parseDuration is divided by 1000 before being passed in. A "5m" delay therefore fires after 0.3 seconds, and sub-second values collapse to setTimeout's clamped minimum.

title: Publish does not handle Slug returning "", producing the bare collection URL
rationale: Slug's documented contract requires callers to check for an empty result, and Publish does not. A title with no letters or digits ("???") yields URL "/posts/", the bare collection URL, so every such post is published at the same page and the old unique-per-id guarantee is silently lost on a reachable path.

title: Receipt enqueued inside the transaction can run before the order commits
rationale: ReceiptMailer.receipt(order).deliver_later enqueues its job on a separate connection while the Order transaction is still uncommitted, so the job can run before the commit and fail with RecordNotFound for an order that does not exist yet. The mailer's documented contract explicitly requires enqueueing after commit.

title: Cleanup forwards an empty Filter, which deletes every upload
rationale: DeleteWhere's contract states an empty Filter deletes every row and that callers building a filter from optional input must refuse an empty one; this handler does not. A single request to DELETE /admin/uploads with no parameters — an operator who omits the query string, or a client that drops it — deletes all uploads. Given the operation is an unconditional, unrecoverable delete, that is a critical data-loss path.

title: User-supplied filename passed to save() without the exists() guard its contract requires, silently destroying existing uploads
rationale: The endpoint passes the client-controlled filename straight to save(), which silently destroys any existing file at that path when the same name is uploaded again, while still returning 201. Uploading a second attachment with a previously used filename permanently overwrites the first user's data.

title: Filename validation misses embedded null bytes, so such requests raise an unhandled ValueError instead of returning 400
rationale: A filename containing an embedded null byte passes the empty/dot check, and open() inside save() then raises ValueError, so the request fails with an unhandled exception instead of the 400 this validation exists to produce.
